docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Silence loses the motion. If you don’t file a response within the time allowed, the motion is decided as uncontested and ordinarily granted without further notice. A motion that lacks a required brief may be summarily denied. (LR 7.3(k))

docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Response time depends on the motion. Responses are due 21 days after service, 30 days for summary judgment, and 14 days for discovery motions. Replies are due 14 days after the response, or 7 days for discovery motions, and are limited to matters newly raised. (LR 7.3(f), (h))

docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Summary judgment starts with a notice. File a notice of intention to file a dispositive motion within 14 days after discovery closes. File the motion and brief within 30 days after discovery closes. All summary judgment issues must go in a single motion and brief unless the court allows otherwise. (LR 56.1(a)–(b))

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Don’t file a motion to strike evidence
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Don’t file a motion to strike evidence. Make an evidentiary objection in your response or reply instead. A separate motion to strike may be summarily denied. (LR 7.6)

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Sealing is disfavored
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Sealing is disfavored. Nothing is filed under seal unless a statute, rule, or order allows it, and filing a document under temporary seal pending a motion is allowed only as LR 5.4 and 5.5 provide. Overbroad or unsupported sealing motions can draw sanctions, including fees. (LR 5.4(a))

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Tell the court early if sealed filings are likely

docs.x: D. Alaska. Page limits: 20 pages, or 5,700 words. Motion and opposition memoranda can’t exceed 20 pages or 5,700 words, and replies can’t exceed 10 pages or 2,750 words. docs.t: D. Alaska — Non-dispositive motions not answered may be summarily decided

docs.t: D. Alaska — Reconsideration is limited to 5 pages, and only for specific reasons

docs.t: D. Kan. — Register by June 30 every year, $25
docs.x: D. Kan.. Register by June 30 every year, $25. Complete annual registration on the online portal and pay the annual fee by June 30. Registration certifies your CLE hours and that you’ve read the local rules. Payment on or after July 1 adds a $100 late fee before reinstatement. Pro hac vice lawyers and court employees are exempt, and a lawyer admitted after January 1 isn’t charged for the first period. The fee is $25 per the FJC’s 2024 compilation. (D. Kan. Rule 83.5.3)

docs.x: D. Kan.. Page limits: 15, but 10 for discovery and 40 for summary judgment. Most briefs run 15 pages with 5-page replies. Discovery-related briefs run 10 with 3-page replies, and summary judgment and class certification briefs run 40 with 15-page replies. A motion to exceed them is due at least 3 days before the brief. docs.x: D. Kan.. Response clocks depend on the motion. Dispositive-type motions get 21 days to respond and 14 to reply. Everything else gets 14 and 7. A late response means the motion is decided as uncontested and ordinarily granted (Rule 7.1(c)). (D. Kan. Rule 6.1(d))

docs.x: D. Kan.. Call the judge before a discovery motion. After a real conversation to confer, which a letter or email doesn’t satisfy, arrange a telephone conference with the judge and opposing counsel. Don’t file or submit the dispute beforehand unless the court asks. (D. Kan. Rule 37.1(a), 37.2)

docs.t: D. Kan. — Discovery motions are due in 30 days
docs.x: D. Kan.. Discovery motions are due in 30 days. File within 30 days of the default or of the response, objection, or disclosure at issue, or the court may deny it as untimely unless you show diligence. (D. Kan. Rule 37.1(c))

docs.t: D. Kan. — Extension motions: 3 days ahead, with specifics
docs.x: D. Kan.. Extension motions: 3 days ahead, with specifics. File at least 3 days before the deadline, stating consultation and views, when the act was first due, prior extensions, and cause. Stipulations that move discovery, hearing, pretrial, or trial dates need court approval and good cause. (D. Kan. Rule 6.1(a), (c))

docs.t: D. Kan. — Pro hac vice counsel can’t e-file
docs.x: D. Kan.. Pro hac vice counsel can’t e-file. Local counsel moves for admission, you pay $50 per case, and local counsel signs every filing and participates meaningfully. Pro hac vice attorneys can’t file electronically unless they work for the United States. (D. Kan. Rule 5.4.1(b), 83.5.4)

docs.t: D. Kan. — Sealing runs on a short clock
docs.x: D. Kan.. Sealing runs on a short clock. A provisional sealed filing is followed by a notice of proposed sealed record. A motion to seal is due 7 days later, a response in 3, and a reply in 1. Stipulations alone don’t justify sealing, and a missed deadline waives the claim. (D. Kan. Rule 5.4.2)

docs.x: M.D. Pa.. Every motion needs a concurrence certificate and a proposed order. docs.t: N.D. Ga. — The pretrial order is due 30 days after discovery

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Briefs: FRAP’s lengths apply
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Briefs: FRAP’s lengths apply. The First Circuit’s local rules don’t change the length limits, so a principal brief is 13,000 words (30 pages) and a reply 6,500 (15 pages). A motion to file an oversized opening brief must be filed at least 10 days before the due date, an oversized reply at least 7 days, and each must state the length sought and be supported by a detailed statement of grounds. The court grants them only for compelling reasons. (FRAP 32(a)(7); 1st Cir. R. 32.4)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — 14-point type
docs.x: 1st Cir.. 14-point type. FRAP 32(a)(5) requires a proportionally spaced serif face of 14 points or larger. (FRAP 32(a)(5))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Briefing dates follow FRAP 31(a)
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Briefing dates follow FRAP 31(a). Schedules are set once the record, including any transcripts, is complete. The appellant has 40 days, the appellee 30, and the reply 21 and at least 7 days before argument. A reply may be rejected if it repeats the main brief or contains matter that belonged in it. Unavailability of a transcript is cause for an extension, subject to the 14-day transcript-ordering rule. (1st Cir. R. 31.0(a))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — The appellant’s brief carries a bound addendum
docs.x: 1st Cir.. The appellant’s brief carries a bound addendum. The addendum goes at the rear of the appellant’s brief with a table of contents. It must include the judgments, rulings, or orders appealed from with their supporting explanation, and the lower-level decision if the court below was reviewing one, such as a magistrate judge’s recommended decision or an ALJ’s initial decision. If the ruling is a text-only docket entry, include that docket page. It may also include up to 25 pages of record excerpts, not counting statutes and rules. The appellee may add an addendum for omitted material on the same terms. Sealed items, including presentence reports and statements of reasons, go in a separate sealed addendum. (1st Cir. R. 28.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Paper covers are color-coded
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Paper covers are color-coded. Appellant is blue, appellee red, intervenor or amicus green, and reply gray. In a cross-appeal the first brief is blue, the second red, the third yellow, and the fourth gray. (FRAP 32(a)(2); court checklist)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — File your appearance within 14 days
docs.x: 1st Cir.. File your appearance within 14 days. Counsel for both sides must file a notice of appearance within 14 days after the case opens. New or additional counsel can appear later, but not after the appellee’s brief is filed without leave. You can’t file pleadings until your appearance is on file. (LR 12.0(a))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Sealed material goes in paper, in its own volume
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Sealed material goes in paper, in its own volume. Briefs are public documents. Sealed or confidential material is filed in paper only, as a separate volume marked “SEALED,” with a motion for leave to file under seal. (LR 28.1; court checklist)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — File the docketing statement within 14 days, and pay the fee
docs.x: 1st Cir.. File the docketing statement within 14 days, and pay the fee. Within 14 days after docketing, the person taking the appeal submits a separate statement listing all parties, last known counsel, and their addresses and emails, on the clerk’s form, and serves it. The other side reports inaccuracies in writing within 14 days. If the appellant doesn’t pay the docket fee within 14 days of the notice of appeal, or misses the statement or another deadline, the appeal may be dismissed for want of diligent prosecution. (1st Cir. R. 3.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Order the transcript within 14 days; the court would rather you didn’t
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Order the transcript within 14 days; the court would rather you didn’t. Use the court’s Transcript Order/Report within 14 days of the notice of appeal, and CJA form 24 if the government pays. A late order can mean dismissal. The court thinks many cases don’t need transcripts and urges stipulations, but the 14-day rule isn’t suspended unless the court orders it for good cause. (1st Cir. R. 10.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Appearances: 14 days, and none after the appellee’s brief without leave
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Appearances: 14 days, and none after the appellee’s brief without leave. Both sides file the appearance form within 14 days after docketing. No lawyer may appear after the appellee’s brief is filed without leave. To file motions or briefs or argue, a lawyer must be admitted and have filed an appearance, and a member of a bar listed in FRAP 46(a) can have the appearance entered subject to applying for admission. No lawyer may withdraw without the court’s consent. (1st Cir. R. 12.0, 46.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Defaults dismiss the appellant and silence the appellee
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Defaults dismiss the appellant and silence the appellee. If the appellant defaults on the brief or required appendix, the clerk dismisses the appeal, and a motion to set it aside must be filed within 14 days showing special circumstances. A defaulting appellee won’t be heard at argument except by leave. (1st Cir. R. 45.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Sealing: paper motion, labeled, and think small
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Sealing: paper motion, labeled, and think small. Material sealed below stays sealed here. To seal anything else, file a paper motion explaining the basis and duration, stamp the item “FILED UNDER SEAL,” and don’t rely on agreement. Sealed material doesn’t go in the regular appendix but in a separate, sealed supplemental volume, and counsel should consider putting the sealed discussion in a separate supplemental filing. (1st Cir. R. 11.0(c), (d); 28.1)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Cite state cases twice, and don’t cite unpublished articles
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Cite state cases twice, and don’t cite unpublished articles. State or Commonwealth court citations must give both the official and the National Reporter citation when published in both. Law review articles unpublished when you file can’t be cited without permission. (1st Cir. R. 32.2)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Translations: Puerto Rico opinions need an English version
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Translations: Puerto Rico opinions need an English version. The court won’t receive non-English documents or cited opinions without translations, and an opinion of a Commonwealth of Puerto Rico court that doesn’t appear in English in the bound volumes needs an official, certified, or stipulated translation. Partial translations must be submitted at least 30 days before argument if only one side submits them. (1st Cir. R. 30.0(e))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Emergency motions: move promptly or risk denial
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Emergency motions: move promptly or risk denial. Motions for a stay or other emergency relief may be denied for failure to present them promptly. If you may need emergency action while the Clerk’s Office is closed, consult the Clerk’s Office at the earliest opportunity; failing to consult may delay action. (1st Cir. L.R. 27.0(b); FRAP 8, 27)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Filing deadline: midnight Eastern (Boston)
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Filing deadline: midnight Eastern (Boston). For electronic filing in the court of appeals the day ends at midnight in the time zone of the circuit clerk’s office in Boston. (FRAP 26(a)(4)(B); 1st Cir. R. 25.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of federal bar rules lists none either. A court can add one by General Order after our sources, as E.D. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)
